entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Srei Reachea (b. 1437, d. 1484) was a monarch of the Khmer Empire during its late Angkorian period, whose reign was marked by intense dynastic struggle and the continued decentralization of royal power. As a son of King Ponhea Yat and a brother to King Reachea Ramathipadi, Srei Reachea was a central figure in the succession conflicts that plagued the Khmer kingdom in the 15th century, a period critical to the eventual abandonment of Angkor as the primary seat of power. His actions and ambitions directly contributed to the volatile political landscape that redefined the Khmer state's geographical and administrative focus.

Srei Reachea's ascent to the throne involved the overthrow of his brother, Reachea Ramathipadi, in 1475, illustrating the deep-seated rivalries within the royal family. His rule, which lasted until 1484, saw the Khmer kingdom grappling with both internal strife and persistent external pressure from the neighboring Ayutthaya Kingdom. While he engaged in military efforts to consolidate power and defend the realm, the constant warfare and internal divisions prevented any lasting stability. This period solidified the trend of the Khmer capital moving away from Angkor, a process initiated by his father, reflecting a pragmatic response to both internal challenges and external threats.
